questions.problem:
The average duration (in minutes) of the videos produced by a popular content creator is $35\,\text{min}.$ Also, $5%$ of their videos have a duration of less than $20$ minutes. Assuming that the duration of the videos is normally distributed, find the standard deviation of the duration times, rounded to the near minute.

*Hint: A table of values of ${Φ}^{-1}(p)$ for different values of $p$ is given below, where $p=Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution.*

| $p$ | $\,0.01\,$ | $\,0.03\,$ | $\,0.05\,$ | $\,0.10\,$ | $\,0.15\,$ | $\,0.20\,$ | $\,0.25\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ${Φ}^{-1}(p)$ | $\,-2.3263\,$ | $\,-1.8808\,$ | $\,-1.6449\,$ | $\,-1.2816\,$ | $\,-1.0364\,$ | $\,-0.8416\,$ | $\,-0.6745\,$ |
questions.worked_solution:
Let $X$ represent the duration of a video. Then we have $X∼N(35,{\sigma }^{2}),$ and we want to find the standard deviation $\sigma .$ 

We know that $P(X\le 20)=0.05.$ Converting $X$ to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\le 20) & =0.05 \\ P(Z\le \frac{20-35}{\sigma }) & =0.05 \\ Φ(-\frac{15}{\sigma }) & =0.05 \\ -\frac{15}{\sigma } & ={Φ}^{-1}(0.05).\end{aligned}
$$

From the table, 

$$
{Φ}^{-1}(0.05)=-1.6449.
$$

Finally then, 

$$
\begin{aligned}-\frac{15}{\sigma } & =-1.6449 \\ \frac{1}{\sigma } & =0.1097 \\ \sigma  & ≈9\,\text{minutes}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
The diameter of the kibble of a particular cat food brand is normally distributed with a mean of $\mu $ and a standard deviation of $0.7\,\text{mm}.$ Additionally, the diameter of $20%$ of kibbles is less than $4.4\,\text{mm}$ in diameter. Find the percentage of kibbles whose diameter is less than $4\,\text{mm},$ rounded to $1$ decimal place.

*Hint: A table of values of ${Φ}^{-1}(p)$ for different values of $p$ is given below, where $p=Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution. *

| $p$ | $\,0.01\,$ | $\,0.03\,$ | $\,0.05\,$ | $\,0.10\,$ | $\,0.15\,$ | $\,0.20\,$ | $\,0.25\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ${Φ}^{-1}(p)$ | $\,-2.3263\,$ | $\,-1.8808\,$ | $\,-1.6449\,$ | $\,-1.2816\,$ | $\,-1.0364\,$ | $\,-0.8416\,$ | $\,-0.6745\,$ |

$$

$$

*In addition, you're given the following table of values for $p=Φ(z)$*.

| $z$ | $\,0.00\,$ | $\,0.01\,$ | $\,0.02\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,-1.4\,$ | $\,0.0808\,$ | $\,0.0793\,$ | $\,0.0778\,$ |
| $\,-1.3\,$ | $\,0.0968\,$ | $\,0.0951\,$ | $\,0.0934\,$ |
| $\,-1.2\,$ | $\,0.1151\,$ | $\,0.1131\,$ | $\,0.1112\,$ |
questions.worked_solution:
Let $X$ represent the diameter of a randomly selected kibble. Then we have $X∼N(\mu ,{0.7}^{2}),$ and we want to find the $P(X<4).$

We know that $P(X<4.4)=0.20.$ First, we convert $X$ to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X<4.4) & =0.20 \\ P(Z<\frac{4.4-\mu }{0.7}) & =0.20 \\ Φ(\frac{4.4-\mu }{0.7}) & =0.20 \\ \frac{4.4-\mu }{0.7} & ={Φ}^{-1}(0.20)\end{aligned}
$$

From the table, 

$$
{Φ}^{-1}(0.20)≈-0.8416.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{4.4-\mu }{0.7} & =-0.8416 \\ 4.4-\mu  & =-0.58912 \\ \mu  & =4.98912\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can solve for $P(X<4)$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X<4) & =P(X\le 4) \\  & =P(Z\le \frac{4-4.98912}{0.7}) \\  & ≈P(Z\le -1.41) \\  & =0.0793 \\  & ≈7.9%\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, approximately $7.9%$ of kibbles are less than $4\,\text{mm}$ in diameter.

questions.worked_solution:
Let $X$ represent the rod length (in centimeters). Then we have $X∼N(100,{4}^{2}).$

We want to find $P(96.8\le X<102.4).$ First, we convert $X$ to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(96.8\le X<102.4) & =P(\frac{96.8-100}{4}\le Z<\frac{102.4-100}{4}) \\  & =P(-0.80\le Z<0.60)\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we express the required probability in terms of $Φ(z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}P(-0.80\le Z<0.60) & =P(Z<0.60)-P(Z<-0.80) \\  & =P(Z\le 0.60)-P(Z\le -0.80) \\  & =Φ(0.60)-Φ(-0.80)\end{aligned}
$$

From the $z$-table, we see that

$$
\begin{aligned}Φ(0.60) & =0.7257 \\ Φ(-0.80) & =0.2119.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(-0.80<Z<0.60) & =Φ(0.60)-Φ(-0.80) \\  & =0.7257-0.2119 \\  & =0.5138 \\  & ≈0.51\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the probability that a randomly selected rod is longer or equal to $96.8\,cm$ but shorter than $102.4\,cm$ is approximately $0.51.$

questions.problem:
The flight times of a particular drone model are normally distributed with a mean of $35$ minutes and a standard deviation of $4$ minutes. What is the probability that a randomly selected drone flies more than $40.08$ minutes on a single charge? **Round your answer to two decimal places.**

*Hint: A table of values of $Φ(z)$ for different values of $z$ is given below, where $Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution.*

| $z$ | $\,0.05\,$ | $\,0.06\,$ | $\,0.07\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,1.1\,$ | $\,0.8749\,$ | $\,0.8770\,$ | $\,0.8790\,$ |
| $\,1.2\,$ | $\,0.8944\,$ | $\,0.8962\,$ | $\,0.8980\,$ |
| $\,1.3\,$ | $\,0.9115\,$ | $\,0.9131\,$ | $\,0.9147\,$ |

The probability that a randomly selected drone flies more than $40.08$ minutes on a single charge is approximately
{{field-1}}.
questions.worked_solution:
Let $X$ represent the drone flight time (in minutes). Then we have $X∼N(35,{4}^{2}).$

We want to find $P(X>40.08).$ Thus, we convert $X$ to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X>40.08) & =P(Z>\frac{40.08-35}{4}) \\  & =P(Z>1.27) \\  & =1-P(Z\le 1.27) \\  & =1-Φ(1.27)\end{aligned}
$$

From the $z$-table, we see that

$$
1-Φ(1.27)=1-0.8980≈0.10.
$$

Therefore, the probability that a randomly selected drone flies more than $40.08$ minutes on a single charge is approximately $0.10.$

questions.problem:
The fasting glucose level of a clinic’s patients is normally distributed with a mean of $\mu \,\text{mg/dL}$ and a standard deviation of $15\,\text{mg/dL}.$ Additionally, $60%$ of the patients have a glucose level between $0.92\mu \,\text{mg/dL}$ and $1.08\mu \,\text{mg/dL}.$ Find the percentage of patients with a fasting glucose lower than $130\,\text{mg/dL}.$ **Round your answer to two decimal places.**

*Hint: A table of values of ${Φ}^{-1}(p)$ for different values of $p$ is given below, where $p=Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution. *

| $p$ | $\,0.75\,$ | $\,0.80\,$ | $\,0.85\,$ | $\,0.90\,$ | $\,0.95\,$ | $\,0.99\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ${Φ}^{-1}(p)$ | $\,0.6745\,$ | $\,0.8416\,$ | $\,1.0364\,$ | $\,1.2816\,$ | $\,1.6449\,$ | $\,2.3263\,$ |

$$

$$

*In addition, you're given the following table of values for $p=Φ(z)$*.

| $z$ | $\,0.04\,$ | $\,0.05\,$ | $\,0.06\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,-1.9\,$ | $\,0.0262\,$ | $\,0.0256\,$ | $\,0.0250\,$ |
| $\,-1.8\,$ | $\,0.0329\,$ | $\,0.0322\,$ | $\,0.0314\,$ |
| $\,-1.7\,$ | $\,0.0409\,$ | $\,0.0401\,$ | $\,0.0392\,$ |

Approximately
{{field-1}}$%$ of the patients have a fasting glucose lower than $130\,\text{mg/dL}.$
questions.worked_solution:
Let $X$ represent the fasting glucose level of a randomly selected patient. Then we have $X∼N(\mu ,{15}^{2}),$ and we want to find $P(X<130).$ But first, we need to find the mean $\mu .$ 

We know that $P(0.92\mu <X<1.08\mu )=0.60.$ First, we convert this to a cumulative probability:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(0.92\mu <X<1.08\mu ) & =0.60 \\ 2P(\mu <X<1.08\mu ) & =0.60 \\ P(\mu <X<1.08\mu ) & =0.30 \\ P(X<\mu )+P(\mu <X<1.08\mu ) & =0.5+0.30 \\ P(X<1.08\mu ) & =0.80\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we convert $X$ to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring. We get

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X<1.08\mu ) & =0.80 \\ P(Z<\frac{0.08\mu }{15}) & =0.80 \\ Φ(\frac{0.08\mu }{15}) & =0.80 \\ \frac{0.08\mu }{15} & ={Φ}^{-1}(0.80).\end{aligned}
$$

From the table, 

$$
{Φ}^{-1}(0.80)=0.8416.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{0.08\mu }{15} & =0.8416 \\ 0.08\mu  & =12.624 \\ \mu  & =\frac{12.624}{0.08} \\  & ≈157.80.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can solve for $P(X<130)$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X<130) & =P(Z<\frac{130-157.80}{15}) \\  & ≈P(Z<-1.85) \\  & =Φ(-1.85) \\  & =0.0322 \\  & ≈3.22%\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, approximately $3.22%$ of the patients have a fasting glucose lower than $130\,\text{mg/dL}.$
